name: fmt
description: Formatted output functions.  printf, sprintf and fprintf take one value per conversion from under the format string, the first value deepest: `%d %i %x %X %o %u %c` an i64, `%f %e %E %g %G` an f64 (an i64 widens), `%s` a str and `%p` a ptr. `%%` is a percent sign. Flags, width and precision work as in C; a length modifier such as `l` is accepted and ignored. Too few values, or one of the wrong type, is a runtime error, raised before anything is taken off the stack.

functions.name: eprintln
functions.description: Print a string to stderr followed by a newline.

functions.name: fprintf
functions.description: Print formatted output to a file descriptor. The values go under the fd, as for printf they go under the format. Anything still buffered for stdout or stderr is written first.

functions.name: println
functions.description: Print a string to stdout followed by a newline.

functions.name: print
functions.description: Print a string to stdout (no newline appended).

functions.name: sprintf
functions.description: Format a string with printf-style specifiers.

functions.name: sprintln
functions.description: Append a newline to a string and return the result.
